transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Janelle (Redwood CSM), Rajesh (Pelagic Procurement), Leah (Pelagic Legal), Omar (Pelagic CTO), Maya (Pelagic Cloud)

Summary:
Quick intake to unblock pricing committee and clarify MSA/DPA exceptions. Main constraints: data residency for EU customers, KMS integration for keys, and a single-year committed spend for Dedicated. Customer needs escalation path for SLA and an audit log for privileged requests.

Topics covered:
- Pricing committee timing and approval hurdles
- MSA redlines Pelagic typically asks for (liability caps, indemnity, audit rights)
- DPA and data residency: in-country processing and subprocessors
- KMS/HSM / Bring-your-own-key options and key rotation
- SLA levels for Dedicated vs Hosted and remediation/credits
- Pilot scoping and acceptance criteria for go-live

Transcript body:
00:00:03 Sofia: okay, thanks everybody for joining, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, i'm the account exec on this one. thanks for the time.
00:00:10 Rajesh: yeah thanks, we -- appreciate it. we wanted to get the legal and procurement lanes aligned before we go to the pricing committee, because last time things stalled at the MSA redlines.
00:00:20 Sofia: totally, that's the goal. Marco from our solutions team is here to go into the technical pieces. Janelle's on for onboarding and pilots. can each of you quick introduce?
00:00:30 Leah: this is leah, counsel, i'll be shepherding the MSA/DPA review on our side. quick note: we have a standard clause set, and i'll flag the parts we usually push back on.
00:00:40 Marco: hey everyone, marco, se — i'll talk infra choices and kms integration.
00:00:44 Omar: omar, cto. i'm mostly here for the architecture constraints: strict EU residency for some data sets and HSM-backed keys for secrets.
00:00:52 Maya: maya, cloud architect, will be doing the preflight and wants to validate network flows.
00:00:57 Sofia: great. Rajesh, can you summarize the approval gating? what's the next internal milestone?
00:01:03 Rajesh: pricing committee next tuesday, if procurement can present expected tco and a recommended path (hosted pilot vs dedicated). legal needs a view on MSA exceptions they expect to permit. without that, they won't greenlight the financials.
00:01:16 Sofia: understood. I'll send our MSA plus callouts. Leah, what are your top 2 non-negotiables?
00:01:22 Leah: liability cap — we typically ask for a 3x cap or a commercial cap tied to fees; we also insist on audit rights and a right to terminate for data incidents. DPA: subprocessors must be listed and we require in-country processing for eu-resident personal data.
00:01:38 Marco: quick clarifying q: the in-country processing, is that all inference traffic or just PII storage?
00:01:44 Leah: primarily any PII at rest or any persisted KV cache containing identifiable info. ephemeral inference may be allowed outside but we need clear guarantees.
00:01:53 Omar: we can design prompts to strip PII, but there will be cases where customer-supplied data is sensitive. we want a BYOK option so keys never leave our environment.
00:02:03 Marco: we support BYOK for Redwood Private and Dedicated via KMS integrations — HSM support is possible in our private offering, requires an ops runbook. for hosted, we have a managed KMS option but not HSM.
00:02:15 Maya: and can we rotate keys monthly? our platform policy enforces rotation every 30 days for certain namespaces.
00:02:21 Marco: yes, key rotation scheduling is supported, but for HSM-backed flows we need to coordinate on ops windows.
00:02:27 Rajesh: on pricing — procurement will push back on long-term committments. do you have a month-to-month hosted with a trial?
00:02:34 Sofia: hosted is pay-as-you-go; pilot can be month-to-month. Dedicated requires a reserved pool and typical terms are 12 months minimum for guaranteed throughput. we can offer a shorter pilot reserved capacity but pricing differs.
00:02:45 Leah: legal will likely ask for termination rights if performance/SLA not met during pilot — a specific acceptance criteria would help.
00:02:53 Janelle: for pilots we usually define success metrics: latency P95 thresholds, throughput targets, and model quality checks against your eval set. we can run a 4-week pilot with weekly checkpoints.
00:03:06 Omar: acceptable. can the pilot include a canary region in eu-west-1 only? we need to prove eu-residency.
00:03:12 Marco: absolutely, we can pin the pilot to eu-west-1 and ensure no routing outside that region. caveat: if you need private peering and private deployment we'll need network setup.
00:03:22 Maya: peering and VPC are necessary for us; we'll require BGP and specific egress IPs for our allowlists.
00:03:28 Marco: documented and supported.
00:03:31 Rajesh: back to pricing committee — they'll want to see all exceptions we expect in an MSA. Leah, what redlines will you definitely ask for?
00:03:38 Leah: short list: 1) increase liability cap 2) add a 30-day termination for material breach 3) audit rights with limited frequency 4) stronger data residency assurances and subprocessor transparency. we're open to a mutual compromise but need those in principle.
00:03:53 Sofia: we can propose narrowing liability exposure on both sides, and provide an escrow statement for model artifacts if that's helpful.
00:04:01 Leah: escrow for model artifacts is interesting; we also care about data escrow for logs in event of termination.
00:04:08 Sofia: we have a standard data retention/escrow playbook — i'll include a short note.
00:04:12 Rajesh: billing question: how do credits apply if SLA misses? we need a deterministic formula to show finance.
00:04:18 Marco: our SLA credit is a percentage of monthly fees based on downtime windows; for dedicated we also include credits for sustained latency breaches. i'll share the exact schedule after the call.
00:04:28 Rajesh: finance needs the numbers in the pricing packet. Sofia, can you include sample invoices or rate cards?
00:04:33 Sofia: yes, we'll put together a redlined packet: rate-card, pilot pricing, and a projection for 12-month reserved vs hosted spend.
00:04:40 Maya: security: are you SOC2 & ISO aligned? also do you have penetration test reports?
00:04:45 Marco: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and working on ISO 27001; we publish a security pack and pen test summaries under NDA.
00:04:52 Leah: we'll need pen test results and a standard SOC attestation. also, where are the logs stored and what retention?
00:04:58 Marco: operational logs stored in region by default with configurable retention. for dedicated/private we can set retention windows per account.
00:05:06 Omar: about RBAC and privileged access for Redwood ops during incidents — we require audit trails showing who accessed what model or keys.
00:05:14 Marco: we provide audit logs for privileged actions; integration with your SIEM is supported via syslog or S3 export.
00:05:20 Leah: ok good. we're also going to check the indemnity language; do you carry cyber insurance and what's the limit?
00:05:27 Sofia: yes, we carry cyber insurance; i'll include the policy summary and limits.
00:05:31 Rajesh: timeline wise, if legal provides a list of exceptions by end of week, we can brief pricing on monday. can we do that?
00:05:38 Leah: yes, we'll try to consolidate our asks into a short checklist by friday.
00:05:42 Janelle: i'll coordinate the pilot scope doc — i'll propose acceptance tests and a weekly report template.
00:05:48 Omar: we also want to run a short performance benchmark against our payloads — 10k concurrent small requests and 100 qps larger prompts to see the memory/kv cache behavior.
00:05:58 Marco: we can run those with a synthetic harness; please share representative prompt sizes and sequence lengths, and we'll replicate.
00:06:05 Maya: we'll send examples.
00:06:08 Sofia: great. wanted to surface one procurement wrinkle: finance may ask for a self-bill arrangement and an invoice net-60 request. our standard is net-30; any thoughts?
00:06:18 Rajesh: we typically push for net-60 for smaller vendors, but for a strategic platform we may accept net-30 if we have a committed volume and forecasting. procurement will prefer net-60 to smooth cash.
00:06:28 Sofia: understood — we'll note both options in the packet.
00:06:31 Leah: also, about escrow — define the trigger events for data escrow release; we need a clear set of conditions.
00:06:37 Sofia: we'll propose standard triggers: insolvency, material breach, decommissioning. we can add a clause for dispute resolution prior to release.
00:06:46 Rajesh: on subprocessor listing, will you provide a rolling list or a fixed list?
00:06:50 Marco: we publish a subprocessors page and provide notice and an objection window before onboarding new subprocessors. for dedicated we can lock down subprocessors.
00:06:59 Leah: objection windows are good, but we often want the ability to onboard with specific security attestations rather than block.
00:07:05 Marco: that's reasonable.
00:07:07 Sofia: switching to SLA specifics: for dedicated, what's the P95 token latency SLA?
00:07:12 Marco: our target SLA for dedicated is P95 under 200ms for typical short-context gen; that can vary with sequence length. we document baseline benchmarks by model and seq length.
00:07:22 Omar: how do you measure that? are you using synthetic sampling or customer-shaped traffic?
00:07:26 Marco: both — we provide baseline synthetic, and for pilots we run replayed traces from your traffic so metrics reflect production.
00:07:33 Rajesh: are there any price cliffs when we add more reserved capacity? finance will look at unit costs.
00:07:38 Sofia: reserved capacity has step discounts at commit thresholds; we'll include a matrix. there's also an option for burst capacity on pay-as-you-go.
00:07:46 Omar: about data deletion — if we instruct you to purge certain datasets, what's the SL for deletion from backups and logs?
00:07:53 Marco: we have deletion strategies; for most hosted flows backups may take 30-90 days to expire. for dedicated/private we can provide accelerated deletion and certify it.
00:08:02 Leah: that's a sticking point; we will flag the retention windows and ask for contractual SLAs for purge if it's PII.
00:08:09 Sofia: we'll highlight the retention differences between hosted and dedicated so procurement can see tradeoffs.
00:08:14 Rajesh: one more — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning?
00:08:19 Marco: yes SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; for private we can do SSO over the private network.
00:08:24 Maya: need a sample SAML metadata file to evaluate compatibility.
00:08:28 Marco: will provide that.
00:08:31 Janelle: i'll coordinate the onboarding checklist and handoff with your ops.
00:08:35 Rajesh: ok back to timing — pricing committee on tuesday. if we get the redlines and a price packet on monday we can land an internal signoff by end of week.
00:08:44 Sofia: plan: we send MSA/DPA + price packet monday EOD, legal redlines by friday, SE preflight next wed. sound good?
00:08:52 Leah: yes, but one ask: can you flag any terms you consider non-starters up front? helps us focus.
00:08:59 Sofia: sure — we'll call out the likely negotiation points in the MSA cover note.
00:09:03 Marco: and i'll include the exact SLA credit table and the technical appendix for the pilot testing harness.
00:09:09 Omar: for the benchmark, we need memory/kv usage numbers per prompt size.
00:09:13 Marco: will include those charts.
00:09:16 Rajesh: fine. are there any escalations if legal or procurement stalls? who is the exec sponsor?
00:09:22 Sofia: i'm the AE; our sales engineering manager is Ben Carter — he can escalate to commercial ops. i'll include his contact.
00:09:29 Leah: good.
00:09:31 Janelle: if you want, we can provision a temporary eval account for the pilot in eu-west-1 within 48 hours.
00:09:38 Maya: that would help.
00:09:40 Sofia: note: temporary eval accounts are limited to 10k tokens/hr unless you request a larger pilot.
00:09:47 Omar: will be fine for initial tests; we may ask to ramp later.
00:09:51 ---
00:10:00 [mid-call, deeper negotiation]
00:10:05 Leah: on indemnity — we rarely accept open-ended indemnities. would Redwood consider a carveout or cap tied to commercial insurance?
00:10:12 Sofia: we typically tie indemnity to insured amounts and carve out breaches caused by customer's misuse. we can propose compromise language.
00:10:19 Leah: ok please draft that.
00:10:21 Marco: question for maya: about peering — do you have a direct connect set up for our region or prefer VPN?
00:10:26 Maya: we prefer private interconnect; our security team standardizes on dedicated peering.
00:10:30 Marco: we'll include peering runbook and expected lead times (usually 2-3 weeks).
00:10:36 Rajesh: can Redwood be flexible on termination notice during pilot, like 14 days instead of 30?
00:10:41 Sofia: for pilot, yes we can usually agree to a 14-day exit clause. for production tied reserved contracts it's different.
00:10:47 Leah: good note.
00:10:49 ---
00:11:00 [closing 10 minutes: recap and explicit next steps]
00:11:05 Sofia: recap — action items: sofia to send MSA/DPA + cover note and pricing packet by monday eod; marco to send sla credit table and tech appendix by monday; janelle to draft pilot acceptance tests and onboarding checklist; pelagic to return legal redlines by friday and confirm pricing committee attendees.
00:11:22 Rajesh: agreed. we'll aim for a quick internal sync on friday if any questions.
00:11:27 Leah: we'll try to trim our asks to a small checklist.
00:11:30 Omar: schedule the technical preflight with maya and marco next wed.
00:11:34 Sofia: i'll send invites. any final points?
00:11:36 Maya: please include a sample syslog export schema; i want to validate SIEM mapping.
00:11:41 Marco: will include.
00:11:43 Sofia: perfect. thanks all.
00:11:46 Rajesh: thanks everyone.

[Call ends ~55 minutes — full discussion had recurring cross-talk, some transcription artifacts: 'BYOK' sometimes rendered as 'bee-yok', 'KMS' as 'kay-em-ess']

Post-call notes (auto):
- Procurement's main blocker is the visibility into MSA redlines and a deterministic pricing packet for the committee.
- Legal flagged retention and indemnity as the highest risk items.
- SE to run pilot harness replicating Pelagic traffic and return benchmark and KV/cache memory metrics.

Attachments referenced: 
- MSA template (to be sent)
- DPA extract (to be sent)
- Dedicated vs hosted TCO spreadsheet (Marco)
- Pilot acceptance test template (Janelle)

End of transcript.
